bull.b: Cloudflare combines rapid multi-year revenue expansion with consistently high gross margins, indicating meaningful software economics and strong customer value. This scale can support continued investment in security, developer products, and network capacity while creating a foundation for improving profitability over time.

Strong operating and free cash flow show that Cloudflare’s core business is generating cash despite reported accounting losses. This internally generated liquidity can fund network investment, product development, and customer growth while reducing reliance on external capital to sustain expansion.

A 122% net retention rate and faster growth among large customers demonstrate durable expansion within the installed base. Customers are increasing spending across Cloudflare’s broader platform, supporting recurring revenue growth, stronger account economics, and deeper enterprise relationships.

bear.b: The sharp increase in debt materially raises financial risk while returns on equity remain negative. Higher obligations can reduce flexibility for investment or acquisitions and make sustainable profitability more important, particularly if cash generation weakens or operating performance falls short.

Cloudflare has improved substantially from earlier losses, but it has not yet established consistent GAAP profitability and operating losses re-expanded in the TTM period. This leaves earnings conversion unproven and makes the business more dependent on continued growth and operating leverage.

Recent compression in gross margin and free-cash-flow margin indicates that growth is not translating into steadily improving efficiency across all periods. If these pressures persist, they could limit incremental cash generation and delay the benefits of Cloudflare’s strong revenue scale.
